scope: processor identification, grading, mechanical sorting, and refinery routing

workflow.title: Identify package
workflow.instruction: Photograph the processor intact and classify broad package family such as ceramic, fiber/organic, BGA, pin-grid, or land-grid when evidence supports it.

workflow.title: Check collectible/resale value
workflow.instruction: Older, rare, or functional processors may be worth more intact than as scrap. Check that path before alteration.

workflow.title: Sort by package family
workflow.instruction: Keep ceramic, fiber, BGA, server, and unknown processors in separate labeled groups.

workflow.title: Inspect visible recovery signals
workflow.instruction: Record pins, lids, substrates, exposed contacts, and package construction without assuming precious-metal content from color alone.

workflow.title: Compare buyer categories
workflow.instruction: Compare specialty e-scrap buyer grades and professional refinery terms before any destructive processing.

workflow.title: Preserve assay value
workflow.instruction: Keep lots clean and documented so a buyer or refiner can grade them accurately.

workflow.title: Time-value check
workflow.instruction: Compare sorting labor and any safe mechanical separation against the intact processor lot value.

hazard_policy: Processor precious-metal refining requires controlled professional processes. This lab does not provide garage-scale chemical recipes or uncontrolled thermal processing.
